subject: general
question: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three chances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In high jump competitions, athletes are typically given **three chances** to clear a specific height.
 
• A failed attempt is recorded if the jumper dislodges the bar or makes a foul jump.
 
• If the jumper clears the height on any of the three attempts, they progress to the next height.
 
• Three consecutive failed attempts at any height result in elimination from the competition.
 
• These rules apply to most standard high jump competitions, including those governed by the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Jump Technique**

 
 
• The Fosbury Flop is the most common technique used by high jumpers today.
 
• It involves a curved approach and a backward layout over the bar.
 
 
 
• **Equipment**
 
 
• High jumpers use a fiberglass or carbon fiber crossbar for competition.
 
• Mats or crash pads are used for safety upon landing.
 
 
 
• **Record Holders**
 
 
• The men's world record for high jump is held by Javier Sotomayor of Cuba with a jump of 2.45 meters.
 
• The women's world record is held by Stefka Kostadinova of Bulgaria with a jump of 2.09 meters.
 
 
 
• **Competition Rules**
 
 
• A fair jump is when the jumper clears the bar without knocking it off the supports.
 
• Jumpers must take off from one foot.
 
• Competitions are often governed by the rules of the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).
